enumeration.method: Independent small-cap theorem-environment enumeration and visual comparison of all nine original Theorems.

checks: Nine complete main-text Theorems: 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.5 and 5.1. Theorem 2.1 continues onto page 5; Theorem 5.1 belongs to the main-text proof section. All original statements, including both Theorem 3.2 conclusions, were compared with the PDF.

Seventeen original source entries and nine auxiliary passages preserve generic matrices/SVD, the mixture model, signal/noise matrices and spectrum, cluster size, empirical subspaces, both algorithms, loss, separation, scalar/vector SG conditions, the symmetric model, its estimator and imported Lemma 3.4 assumptions. Original source kinds and terms are retained.

Independent reconstruction yields 45 direct uses and 56 related connections. Algorithm 2 imports only Algorithm 1 step 1; it has no fixed-r clustering-output dependency. Theorem 3.3 uses r=k and inline Gaussian noise, without acquiring the signal-rank or SG interfaces. Theorems 3.1-3.5 do not acquire leave-one-out proof interfaces.

Theorem 3.5 imports Theorem 3.4 assumptions and Lemma 3.4 assumptions/rate (31). The psi_3 definition, scalar variance/proxy restrictions, fixed Delta, density regularity, Fisher information and limit-infimum-supremum order are retained. The lemma is not counted as a Theorem.

Visual checks preserve the square-root scope in (11)-(12), the k^3.5 and power -0.25 in (27), the squared upper/lower corrections of Theorem 3.4, exact argmin algorithms and the largest adaptive index with >=T. Generic matrices remain distinct from mixture matrices.

Nine source issues are recorded without altering quotations, notably the equality/inequality discrepancy in the loss, the sign of the real delta specialization, unspecified SVD endpoint conventions, ratio denominators, threshold wording and empty-set behavior. This is source-faithful census validation, not proof certification.

All seventeen entries have literal natural-language source terms, faithful source headings and symbol selectors checked against their source passage or related same-paper Theorems. All 56 connections have explanations of the actual symbol or scoped reference; no boilerplate relationship captions are used.
All six JSON content artifacts reproduce byte for byte from the retained scripts. The source PDF, independently reviewed inventory and complete artifact set are hash-pinned.

source_notes.description: The definition of ell on page 9 prints I{z_i=phi(z_i*)}, while equation (17) on that same page counts unequal labels. Both original passages are retained. The census does not silently replace equality by inequality or certify consistency of the resulting mathematical claims.

Model (28) allows delta in R. The following commentary writes Delta=2*sqrt(p)*delta and lambda_1=delta*sqrt(n*p), and calls P rank one, without excluding zero or using absolute values. Preserve the model and record this mismatch with nonnegative distance/singular values.

The arbitrary-matrix setup allows r up to min(p,n-1), but Theorems 2.1 and 5.1 use sigma_{r+1}. Mixture matrices similarly use r up to k, and Algorithm 2 uses lambda-hat_{a+1}. The inspected setup does not explicitly state all dimension restrictions or a general zero-extension convention. Do not silently supply one.

Several displayed ratios divide by residual norms, noise norms, sigma or bar-sigma. The source does not state a universal zero-denominator convention. Retain the ratio hypotheses as printed rather than replacing them by multiplied inequalities or adding positivity assumptions.

Algorithm 2 step 2 says greater than T in prose but uses >=T in formula (23); the following explanation also says greater or equal. Preserve the complete original algorithm with that discrepancy and the largest-index rule.

No fallback for an empty maximization set in (23) appears in the algorithm. Main-text page 14 points to Lemma B.1 for existence under Lemma 3.3 conditions. The appendix is not read, and no unprovided fallback is invented.

The algorithms specify global argmin outputs and SVDs without explicit tie-breaking or measurable-selection rules. Approximate k-means discussed later is not the algorithm stated in the theorem hypotheses.

Theorem 3.5 imports Lemma 3.4, which assumes Delta is a constant and states a p-to-infinity minimax bound up to constants. Preserve that scope and the original optimal-if-and-only-if assertion; do not replace it with a growing-separation asymptotic or claim to have checked the proof.

The source SG definition bounds E exp(tX) directly, for all real t. It does not use E exp(t(X-EX)). Theorem 3.4 distinguishes actual variance bar-sigma squared from proxy sigma squared and requires sigma<=C*bar-sigma; these are not interchangeable.

ambient_resolution.T2.1: Y,Y-hat,y_n and the ordered singular data are D1-D2. Rho is bound in (3); index i is local in the sum. There is no noise-distribution hypothesis and no dependency on the mixture model.
ambient_resolution.T2.2: Mixture observations/noise are D3-D4; beta is D5; empirical subspaces D7; population spectrum and kappa D8. Rho_0 is local; the result is for every sample index. It does not import Theorem 2.1 as a statement prerequisite.
ambient_resolution.T2.3: Same deterministic mixture setup as T2.2, with a locally selected r and tilde-rho_0 defined in (11). The factor sqrt(k^2/(beta*n)) multiplies lambda_{r+1} outside the square root. It does not assume r=kappa.
ambient_resolution.T3.1: Algorithm 1 uses r=kappa, requiring the signal rank D8. Independent zero-mean vector SG noise uses D13. Beta,Delta and ell are D5,D11,D10. Psi_1,rho_1 and the constants are local. No proof-only leave-one-out projection interface is added.
ambient_resolution.T3.2: Algorithm 2 D14 uses threshold T and imports only the SVD step A3. Beta,Delta,ell and vector SG are D5,D11,D10,D13. Psi_2,rho_2 and constants are local; the finite-sample and additional asymptotic conclusions are both retained. Neither signal rank kappa nor the fixed-r Algorithm 1 output is required.
ambient_resolution.T3.3: Algorithm 1 is used with r=k, not r=kappa. Iid isotropic Gaussian noise is explicitly bound in the theorem and uses ambient normal-law notation; it does not make the scalar/vector SG definitions statement dependencies. The displayed divergence, exponent correction and 2*exp(-0.08*n) remain as printed.
ambient_resolution.T3.4: Model (28) is D15, check-z is D16, ell and Delta are D10-D11, beta D5 and scalar SG D12. Psi_3 is the original local ratio A4. Xi, sigma,bar-sigma and the constants are locally quantified. Preserve both squared exponential corrections and all upper/lower tail terms.
ambient_resolution.T3.5: Expand T3.4 assumptions using A5 and its psi_3 lower bound with A4. Expand Lemma 3.4 assumptions using D17 and the referenced rate using A6. The fixed Delta and density conditions are retained; no lemma is counted as a Theorem. The Gaussian-law characterization remains the original conclusion.
ambient_resolution.T5.1: Generic matrix setup D1-D2, as in Section 2.1; the quadratic spectral-gap condition is written locally. This is a labeled main-text Theorem even though it appears in Section 5. No rho>2 hypothesis from T2.1 is imported.

source_claim_references.scope: All assumptions, including model (28), scalar noise restrictions, beta*n>40 and the psi_3 lower bound; not the two risk conclusions.
Positive continuously differentiable mean-zero density, finite Fisher information, fixed Delta and minimax rate (31). Lemma is not an inventoried claim.
Empirical SVD step only, retained in A3; not the fixed-r k-means output.

review_limits: Registered arXiv v2 source; no assumption of equivalence to the published article.
Source discrepancies are retained separately; no appendix-body material is used.
Source and schema validation do not certify mathematical proofs.
